quotes.text: You can apply up to 20 discounts to a subscription, subscription item, or invoice. This limit is shared between  coupons and promotion codes.

To customize how a coupon calculates discounts, configure a [Stripe-authored discount calculation script](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/scripts/stripe-authored/discount-calculation.md) or [author your own discount calculation script](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/scripts/discount-calculation.md).
Duration defaults to `once`, which applies only to the first invoice.
Both actions count toward the same `max_redemptions` limit on the coupon.
Subscriptions apply promotion code and price updates separately, which might cause unexpected updates.

old_evidence.text: You can set up to 20 entries in the `discounts` parameter.
After the invoice that used the coupon is finalized or paid, the subscription’s `discounts` stops showing that discount.
The Accounts v2 API is generally available for Connect users, and in public preview for other Stripe users.

findings: Same canonical coupon guide, May versus November capture. Both explain coupons as discount definitions and promotion codes as customer-facing wrappers, with product restrictions inherited from the parent coupon (new 15-35, 95-107; old 8-21, 81-95). November adds a comparison table separating coupon controls from promotion-code-only customer, first-purchase and minimum-spend restrictions; its examples are illustrative, not eligibility guarantees.

November states a shared maximum of 20 discounts from coupons and promotion codes on a subscription, subscription item or invoice (new 24); May states up to 20 entries per discounts parameter in the stacking section (old 563-571). Current source line 40 and concept lines 10/40 mention subscription and item but omit invoice scope; do not infer a combined 20 total across all three objects from the text.

November adds an optional route to Stripe-authored or self-authored discount calculation scripts (new 91-93), a navigation/capability addition absent in May. The capture gives no script rules or enabled-account claim; keep it a locator rather than infer execution behavior.

Coupon duration remains once, repeating or forever, with backdated duration starting from the backdated subscription start (new 193-207; old 215-229). November explicitly says once is the default and removes the subscription discount after invoice finalization while the invoice retains it (new 195, 199-205). May already described finalization, but also used 'finalized or paid' in an explanatory bullet (old 221-227); retain the dated phrasing without claiming a new runtime transition from the wording change.

November clarifies that directly applying a coupon and redeeming a promotion code both consume the underlying coupon's max_redemptions, with limit across all customers (new 209-215). May described the aggregate coupon cap generally (old 231-235) but did not explicitly state promotion-code redemptions share it.

Promotion code restrictions continue: first-time eligibility excludes initiated even unsuccessful PaymentIntents and trial subscriptions; minimum amount is checked at redemption and applies to initial subscription payment; amount-restricted codes cannot be applied to subscription or invoice items, subscription updates, or future schedule phases (new 229-237, 309-336; old 249-257, 329-356). Do not generalize those restrictions to ordinary coupons.

Accounts v2 customer_account examples remain distinct from Customers v1 customer examples, and Accounts v2 is Connect GA but public preview for others with preview version in that case (new 126-152, 265-283; old 112-162, 285-303). November adds a Dashboard preview enablement instruction (new 130); no captured text verifies a particular account's access.

Stacking still supports subscription and item discounts, order affects mixed amount_off/percent_off, duplicate/same-parent combinations are excluded, updates replace retained entries if omitted, and discount-only updates do not generate prorations (new 430-503; old 474-587). November mainly changes formatting and Node examples to curl, not the documented stacking logic. The Checkout promotion-code parameter link is corrected from object to create documentation (new 423-425; old 467-469).
substantive_changes: The November overview explicitly extends the shared 20-discount statement to invoices as well as subscription and item targets and to both coupons and promotion codes (new 24 versus old 567).
Optional discount calculation scripts are newly routed, without detail about execution or availability (new 91-93).

The November duration section explicitly states default once and describes removal at finalization, while May already documented once and a finalized-or-paid explanatory line (new 195-205; old 219-227). This is clarification, not proof of a changed runtime rule.
Direct coupon application and promotion-code redemption are now explicitly said to share the coupon max_redemptions counter (new 209-215 versus old 231-235).

The November coupon-versus-code table states deleting a coupon archives associated promotion codes (new 26-33); May separately states deletion blocks new uses and invalid underlying coupons permanently inactivate codes (old 195, 398-402), so preserve those distinct effects.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep May Node SDK examples and Accounts v2 preview/version caveat as dated evidence (old 56-66, 112-164, 423-465). November curl rendering does not deprecate Node or prove account eligibility (new 70-76, 126-152, 403-421).

Keep the old coupon-duration description including 'finalized or paid' as dated May text (old 221-227); November uses finalization only (new 199-205), and the snapshots alone do not establish a separate rule change.

Preserve portal caveat that a promotion code can succeed despite a failed price upgrade, product-scope inheritance, first-time restrictions, redemption-time minimum, permanent code inactivity after expiry/max, and update/stacking constraints (old 85-95, 241-257, 331-402, 563-587; new 19-20, 221-237, 309-382, 479-503).
conflicts: wiki/sources/source-stripe-subscriptions-coupons.md:33 and wiki/concepts/stripe-subscriptions-coupons.md:33 state code uniqueness across active codes without the any-customer qualification. Both captures allow duplicate active code strings for distinct customer-restricted promotion codes but forbid reuse by any-customer codes (new 245-261; old 265-281). Narrow those summaries.

wiki/sources/source-stripe-subscriptions-coupons.md:40 and wiki/concepts/stripe-subscriptions-coupons.md:10,40 state the 20-discount limit only for subscription/item; new raw line 24 includes invoice. Add invoice scope while avoiding an inferred global combined cap.

wiki/sources/source-stripe-subscriptions-coupons.md:44 says prorations occur 'only when combined' with another change, which can imply discount updates themselves cause proration. New raw 499-503 and old 583-587 say discount-only changes do not create prorations; combined billable changes trigger them and use updated discount state. Narrow wording.
unresolved_questions: The new script links do not specify eligibility, configuration requirements, or exact discount-calculation behavior; read those destinations before making such claims.
The captured snippets do not prove current Accounts v2 preview access for any particular non-Connect account or universal availability of a code or discount.
The yearly repeating example has slightly different wording between old line 217 and new line 197; the snapshot comparison alone does not establish a change in billing-cycle discount semantics.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/coupons, the November capture describes backend-applied coupons and customer-facing promotion codes that wrap coupons, inherit parent product restrictions, and create Discount objects when redeemed (new lines 15-24; old lines 8-21). It covers once, repeating and forever duration, product eligibility, redemption limits, code eligibility, stacking and update behavior (new 95-109, 193-215, 229-237, 430-503; old 81-95, 215-235, 249-257, 474-587). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-coupons]] summarizes these central mechanisms, but its active-code uniqueness wording omits the customer-restricted duplicate exception (source 33; new 245-261; old 265-281). Accounts v2 examples require the preview version for preview users; Connect users are described as GA (new 126-152; old 112-162).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/coupons, the notable additions are the explicit shared 20-discount limit including invoices (new line 24; old line 567), optional discount-calculation-script links (new 91-93), and explicit shared max_redemptions counting for direct coupon use and promotion-code redemption (new 209-215; old 231-235). The November once-duration default/finalization language clarifies May's account rather than proving a runtime change (new 195-205; old 219-227). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-coupons]] should preserve coupon versus promotion-code restrictions, customer/account variants, stacking order and replacement rules, and the portal price-upgrade warning (new 19-33, 126-152, 221-237, 479-503; old 112-162, 241-257, 563-587). Node-to-curl and image/link changes are presentation or navigation. The reciprocal [[stripe-subscriptions-coupons]] route needs invoice scope and qualified active-code uniqueness; no account eligibility or script behavior follows from the capture.
